---
title: "Explore Gridworld policy iteration"
toc: false
page-layout: full
---

Policy iteration alternates between two operations. First, evaluate the current
policy to obtain its state-value function. Then improve the policy by choosing
the action with the largest one-step return at every state. This page treats
policy evaluation as a completed operation; use the preceding random-policy
explorer to step through its Bellman updates.

$$
\pi_{k+1}(s) \in \arg\max_a
\left[r(s,a,s') + \gamma V^{\pi_k}(s')\right].
$$

::: {.callout-tip}
## What to watch

The left grid holds the current policy $\pi_k$. The right grid holds the
value function that was most recently evaluated. After an improvement, the
right grid is intentionally marked as stale: it still represents
$V^{\pi_k}$, while the left grid has advanced to $\pi_{k+1}$. Evaluate
the new policy to complete the next cycle.
:::

<div id="gridworld-policy-iteration-explorer" class="gridworld-policy-iteration-explorer" aria-label="Interactive Gridworld policy iteration explorer">

    <button id="gridworld-iteration-improve" type="button">Greedy improvement</button>
    <button id="gridworld-iteration-run" type="button">Run to optimum</button>
    <output id="gridworld-iteration-status" class="gridworld-iteration-status" aria-live="polite">Policy π₀ is ready to evaluate.</output>
  </div>

  <section class="gridworld-iteration-cycle" aria-labelledby="gridworld-iteration-cycle-heading">
    <div>
      <h2 id="gridworld-iteration-cycle-heading">Policy-iteration cycle</h2>
      <p>Start from the uniform random policy. Evaluate it, improve it greedily, then evaluate the updated policy.</p>
    </div>
    <ol class="gridworld-iteration-cycle-steps" aria-label="Policy iteration steps">
      <li><strong>1</strong><span>Policy <i>π</i><sub>k</sub></span></li>
      <li><strong>2</strong><span>Evaluate <i>V</i><sup>π<sub>k</sub></sup></span></li>
      <li><strong>3</strong><span>Improve to <i>π</i><sub>k + 1</sub></span></li>

  <div class="gridworld-iteration-workbench">

      </div>
      <div id="gridworld-iteration-policy-grid" class="gridworld-iteration-grid gridworld-iteration-policy-grid" role="grid" aria-label="Current Gridworld policy"></div>
      <p class="gridworld-iteration-grid-note">Arrows show actions with nonzero policy probability. Click a cell to inspect it below.</p>
    </section>

    <section class="gridworld-iteration-panel gridworld-iteration-value-panel" aria-labelledby="gridworld-iteration-value-heading">
      <div class="gridworld-iteration-panel-heading">
        <h2 id="gridworld-iteration-value-heading">State-value function</h2>
        <p id="gridworld-iteration-value-caption">Evaluate π₀ to fill this grid.</p>
      </div>
      <div id="gridworld-iteration-value-grid" class="gridworld-iteration-grid gridworld-iteration-value-grid" role="grid" aria-label="State values for the current or previous policy"></div>
      <div class="gridworld-iteration-legend" aria-label="State value color legend"><span>Lower value</span><i></i><span>Higher value</span></div>

        <h2 id="gridworld-iteration-inspector-heading">Greedy improvement at one state</h2>

        </thead>
        <tbody id="gridworld-iteration-action-values"></tbody>

  <section class="gridworld-iteration-reading" aria-labelledby="gridworld-iteration-reading-heading">
    <h2 id="gridworld-iteration-reading-heading">How to read the explorer</h2>
    <ol>
      <li>Evaluation runs the same synchronous Bellman expectation updates shown on the previous page until the value estimates converge.</li>
      <li>Improvement compares the four values <i>r</i> + γ<i>V</i><sup>π<sub>k</sub></sup>(<i>s</i>′) at every state and replaces the policy with its greedy version.</li>
      <li>If no arrows change during improvement, the policy is stable and therefore optimal for this finite Gridworld.</li>
    </ol>
  </section>
</div>
